newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Kabul ammunition dump blast kills six.
newsitem.headline: Kabul ammunition dump blast kills six.

text.p: An ammunition dump exploded in the Afghan capital Kabul on Wednesday, killing at least six fighters of the purist Islamic Taleban militia, a Pakistan-based Afghan news agency reported.
The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted Taleban officials in Kabul as saying that the casualty toll might rise. Taleban officials had earlier denied there had been any casualties.
There was no immediate word on what had caused the explosion at the ammunition dump in the Bala Hisar district.
AIP said the blast had shattered windows over a wide area, but there were no immediate reports of civilian casualties.
The Taleban have controlled Kabul since capturing it from forces loyal to ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani on September 27.
They are still fighting to extend their strict Islamic rule over opposition-held northern parts of Afghanistan.
